subject: language
intro: Mr. Brooks here. Let's plan a lesson on how point of view shapes a story.

beats.narration: The title asks the question at the center of the lesson.
beats.text: Whose Story Is It? Point of View

beats.narration: This standard asks students to analyze how an author develops and contrasts characters' points of view.
Retelling from a new perspective is the best way to see point of view.
beats.text: Students will be able to analyze how a story changes when told from a different character's point of view.

beats.narration: A picture book is a quick, engaging hook, even in 7th grade.
beats.text: Read "The True Story of the 3 Little Pigs" (told by the wolf). "Does the wolf's version change how you feel about him?"

beats.narration: The live rewrite shows exactly how point of view changes what we know.
beats.text: Model first- vs. third-person narration and limited vs. omniscient. Rewrite one paragraph from the class novel from a different character's view.

beats.narration: The explanation paragraph is where the analysis happens.
beats.text: Students choose a scene from the class novel and rewrite it from another character's point of view, then write a paragraph explaining what changed.

beats.narration: This checks analysis, not just identification.
beats.text: How would the story change if it were told by a different character? Give one specific example.

outro: Picture book, model, rewrite, reflect. Your turn.
